anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: Frozen foundations stay frozen. The existing `v1` strategy, `default` profile, tape engine state vocabulary/thresholds, frozen structure calculations, canonical stores, and archived-era behavior remain additive/versioned, never silently mutated.
anti_goal_violations.evidence: apps/backend/app/research/foundry_hermetic_summary.py:75-82 and :183-188 — production (non-test) code reassigns the frozen Scout internal `scout._two_sided_p = lambda observed, null: 0.0001` and restores it in a `finally`. These are the only two raw reassignments of a `scout` internal anywhere under `apps/backend/app/research/`. The patch executes inside the backend server process at module-import time, because `micro_routes.py:774` builds `_HERMETIC_ORACLES_VIEW` at import. The equivalent test code uses `monkeypatch.setattr` (tests/test_foundry_hermetic_epoch.py:255,465,669), which auto-restores; the production copy does not have that protection. Nothing persists past the `finally` and no research result changed (evaluator re-ran the composite epoch: all 7 plan labels match the real returned foundry_state, denominator/canonical-order/evidence-class flags all true), so this is scored MINOR, not critical. Recorded rather than dismissed in prose per goal.md's own anti-goal 'Anti-goal violations use the existing Goal Mode anti-goal violation state/disposition machinery; they are not dismissed in prose.' Fix: build the fragility fixture from data that genuinely yields a low p-value, or compute the hermetic-oracles summary in an isolated process/lazily instead of patching a frozen module inside the serving process.
